# Owen Ford

## Overview

- **Age:** In his thirties  <sub>[v4 c23 P8](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0008)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c22 P21](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0021)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v4 c40 P12](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0012)</sub>
- **Origin:** Ontario, Canada  <sub>[v4 c22 P21](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0021)</sub>
- **Role:** Author and journalist  <sub>[v4 c22 P21](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0021), [v4 c23 P18](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0018)</sub>

## Appearance

Owen Ford is a tall, broad-shouldered man with a handsome face, well-cut features, and a clean-shaven chin. He has thick brown hair, large, dark-gray eyes, and a very friendly smile showcasing nice teeth. Unsmiling, his expression can appear somewhat sad and absent.

_Sources: [v4 c23 P8](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0008), [v4 c23 P10](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0010)_

## Personality

He possesses a pleasant, delightful smile and a great deal of personal charm. Passionate about his craft, he becomes deeply absorbed in his writing and works with intense dedication once inspired. Although respectful of his moral duties, he experiences deep emotional passion when in love.

_Sources: [v4 c23 P8](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0008), [v4 c25 P11](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0011), [v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002), [v4 c26 P8](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0008)_

- Talented writer  <sub>[v4 c25 P0](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0000), [v4 c25 P13](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0013)</sub>

## Goals

- To find a central motif and write a great Canadian novel  <sub>[v4 c23 P18](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0018), [v4 c23 P20](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0020)</sub>
- To marry Leslie Moore  <sub>[v4 c38 P9](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0009), [v4 c38 P10](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0010)</sub>

## History

Owen Ford came to Four Winds to recover his health after a bout of typhoid fever and boarded with Leslie Moore at the gray house up the brook. Introduced to Captain Jim by Anne Blythe, he discovered Captain Jim's 'life-book' of sea adventures and resolved to use it as the basis for his novel. During his time at Four Winds, he collaborated closely with Captain Jim and spent his afternoons and evenings with Anne, Gilbert, and Leslie, falling deeply in love with Leslie. Believing Leslie to be irrevocably tied to her brain-damaged husband, Dick Moore, he suffered quietly and prepared to leave Four Winds forever. However, after Gilbert urged an operation for Dick, it was revealed that 'Dick' was actually his cousin George Moore and that the real Dick had died years prior. After Leslie became a free woman, Owen returned to Four Winds the following summer. He proposed to Leslie in Anne's garden, and the two became engaged to be married.

_Sources: [v4 c22 P21](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0021), [v4 c24 P17](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0017), [v4 c25 P0](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0000), [v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002), [v4 c26 P20](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0020), [v4 c31 P28](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0028), [v4 c34 P30](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0030), [v4 c38 P0](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0000), [v4 c38 P10](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0010)_

## Background by volume

- Grandson of John Selwyn and Persis Leigh, the original owners of the 'House of Dreams'  <sub>[v4 c22 P21](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0021), [v4 c24 P22](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0022)</sub>
- Raised in Ontario, where his mother Alice Selwyn moved after her marriage  <sub>[v4 c2 P25](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0025), [v4 c24 P22](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0022)</sub>
- Suffered from a severe case of typhoid fever in the spring before visiting Four Winds  <sub>[v4 c22 P21](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0021)</sub>

## Quotes

> A man doesn't have much chance for that sort of thing. I've done a good deal of short story writing for the magazines, but I've never had the leisure that seems to be necessary for the writing of a book. With three months of liberty I ought to make a start, though—if I could only get the necessary motif for it—the SOUL of the book.  <sub>[v4 c23 P20](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0020)</sub>

> Mrs. Blythe, this is a wonderful book—absolutely wonderful. If I could take it and use the material for a book I feel certain I could make the novel of the year out of it.  <sub>[v4 c25 P0](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0000)</sub>

> I loved her from the moment I first saw her standing against the darkness in that glow of light.  <sub>[v4 c26 P16](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0016)</sub>

> These roses are very late—they bloom after all the others have gone—and they hold all the warmth and soul of the summer come to fruition  <sub>[v4 c38 P6](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0006)</sub>
